CAPITOLO XXVII





9 ottobre — Fu nella [[motifs/night|notte]] del 4 ottobre, poco dopo il tè, che.

Annabella stava cantando e suonando, come al solito con [[characters/arthur|Arthur]] al suo fianco.

Dall’altra parte, aveva finito di suonare la sua canzone, ma continuava comunque a sedere davanti allo strumento; e.

Si appoggiava allo schienale della sua sedia, chiacchierando a malapena…

Suoni udibili… con il suo viso molto vicino al suo.

Guardò verso [[characters/lord-lowborough|Lord Lowborough]]. Era all'altra estremità della stanza, a parlare.

Con i signori Hargrave e Grimsby… ma lo vidi correre verso la sua signora.

Un’occhiata rapida e impaziente verso il suo ospite, piena di intensità…

"Disquietude… a sentiment che fece sorridere Grimsby. Deciso ad interromperlo."

_in un incontro ravvicinato_, le [[motifs/rose|rose]], e, selezionando un brano di musica.

Si alzò e si avvicinò al pianoforte, con l’intenzione di chiedere alla signora di suonarlo.

Ma rimasi immobile e senza parole nel vederla seduta lì.

Titolo:  
Ascoltando, con un sorriso apparentemente esultante sul suo viso arrossato…

I suoi dolci sussurri, mentre la sua mano si arrendeva silenziosamente alla sua stretta.

Il [[motifs/blood|sangue]] prima affluì al mio cuore, poi alla mia testa; perché là si trovava.

Più di questo… quasi nel momento in cui mi avvicinavo, lui lanciò un’occhiata affrettata…

Gettò un’occhiata alle altre persone nella stanza.

Con passione premette quella mano inerme sulle sue labbra. Alzando lo sguardo…

Con gli occhi fissi su di me, li abbassò di nuovo, confuso e scoraggiato.

Anche lei mi vide e mi affrontò con uno sguardo di fiera sfida. Io…

La musica al pianoforte… e poi mi ritirai. Mi sentivo male, ma non me ne andai.

La stanza: felicemente, stava facendo tardi, e non sarebbe passato molto tempo…

La compagnia si disperse.



Andai davanti al [[motifs/fire|focolare]] e appoggiai la testa contro il camino. In quel momento.

Un minuto o due… qualcuno mi chiese se mi sentissi male. Non risposi.

Infatti, in quel [[motifs/time|momento]], non sapevo cosa venisse detto; ma ho agito meccanicamente.

Alzò lo sguardo e vide il signor Hargrave in piedi accanto a me sul tappeto.



“Devo portarti un bicchiere di vino?” disse lui.



“No, grazie,” risposi; e, allontanandomi da lui, guardai intorno. Lady…

Accanto al marito

Gli mise una mano sulla spalla, parlava dolcemente e sorrideva mentre lo guardava negli occhi; e

[[characters/arthur|Arthur]] era seduto al tavolo, sfogliando un libro di incisioni. Mi misi a sedere anch'io.

Mi sedetti nella sedia più vicina; e il signor Hargrave, rendendosi conto di essere utile…

Non essendo desiderati, furono saggiamente ritirati. Poco dopo, l’azienda…

Si separarono, e mentre gli ospiti si ritiravano nelle loro stanze, [[characters/arthur|Arthur]].

Si avvicinò a me, sorridendo con la massima sicurezza.



“Sei davvero _molto_ arrabbiata, [[characters/helen|Helen]]?”, mormorò lui.



“Non è uno scherzo, [[characters/arthur|Arthur]]”, dissi seriamente, ma con la massima calma possibile.

"Potresti... a meno che non consideri una barzelletta perdere per sempre il mio affetto."



“Che cosa! Così amaro?” esclamò ridendo, stringendomi la mano tra le sue.

“Tutto suo… ma io l’ho strappato via, pieno di indignazione… quasi di disgusto.”

Evidentemente era sotto l’effetto del vino.



“Allora devo mettermi in ginocchio”, disse; e dopo essersi inginocchiato davanti a me…

Con le mani giunte, sollevate in un’imitazione di umiliazione, continuò…

Con voce supplicante: “Perdona me, [[characters/helen|Helen]], cara [[characters/helen|Helen]], perdonami, e io _mai più_, ”

“Fallo di nuovo!”, e, nascondendo il viso nel fazzoletto, fingeva…

singhiozzò ad alta voce.



Lasciandolo così impegnato, presi la mia candela e, uscendo silenziosamente…

La stanza… Salii di corsa le scale il più velocemente possibile. Ma lui presto se ne accorse.

“Che lo avevo lasciato… e, correndo verso di me, mi abbracciò.”

Appena entrai nella stanza e stavo per chiudere la porta…

Il suo viso.



“No, no, per l’amor del cielo, non riuscirete a sfuggirmi in questo modo!” gridò. Poi, allarmato…

“Nella mia agitazione, lui mi pregò di non lasciarmi prendere da tale passione.”

Dicendomi che avevo il viso bianco e che dovevo uccidermi se lo facessi.



“Lasciami andare, allora”, mormorai; e immediatamente mi lasciò andare…

Era davvero bravo, perché ero veramente presa dalla passione. Mi immersi completamente nella situazione.

"Easy-chair e sforzi per riprendere il controllo di me stesso… volevo parlare."

Lo guardai con calma. Stava al mio fianco, ma non osò toccarmi né fare nulla.

Parlò per qualche secondo; poi, avvicinandosi ancora di più, disse…

In ginocchio, non per simulare [[concepts/humility|umiltà]], ma per mettersi al mio livello.

Appoggiando una mano allo schienale della sedia, cominciò a parlare a bassa voce:

“È tutto assurdo, [[characters/helen|Helen]]. Solo uno scherzo, niente di più. Non vale nemmeno la pena pensarci.”

“Non imparerai mai, vero?”, continuò lui con maggiore audacia, “che…”

Niente di cui aver paura da parte mia. Che ti amo completamente e totalmente. O forse,, ”

“E poi”, aggiunse con un sorriso malizioso, “mi preoccupo mai davvero degli altri…”

Che [[motifs/well|bene]] possa risparmiarlo, perché quelle fantasie arrivano e se ne vanno in un attimo, come un lampo.

La [[motifs/lightning|fulmine]], mentre il mio [[motifs/love|amore]] per te brucia costantemente, e per sempre, come.

Il sole. Tu piccolo, esorbitante [[archetypes/tyrant|tiranno]], non oserai farlo.



“Stai zitto un attimo, per favore, [[characters/arthur|Arthur]]”, dissi, “e ascoltami, ”.

“Non pensare che io sia nel pieno di una rabbia gelosa: sono perfettamente calmo. Senti la mia mano.”

E lo allungai solennemente verso di lui… ma poi lo chiusi sopra il suo.

“Energia che sembrava smentire quell’affermazione… e che lo fece sorridere.” “Tu…”

“Non c’è bisogno di sorridere, signore,” dissi, continuando a stringere la presa e guardandolo negli occhi.

“Tenendolo fermo con determinazione, fino a quando quasi non si arrese davanti a me… ‘Potreste pensare che…’”

“Tutto molto bene, signor Huntingdon… ma divertirsi a provocarmi non è certo la cosa più appropriata.”

[[concepts/jealousy|invidia]]; ma fai attenzione a non suscitare invece il mio odio. E quando tu.

Dopo aver spento una volta il mio [[motifs/love|amore]], scoprirete che non sarà affatto facile riacquistarlo.

“Riaccesilo ancora.”



“Beh, Helen, non ripeterò più quell’offesa. Ma non volevo davvero nulla di male, ”

Vi assicuro: avevo bevuto troppo vino e quasi non ero più me stesso…

“[[motifs/time|tempo]]”.



“Spesso prendi troppo; ed è un’altra abitudine che detesto.” Lui

“Lo guardò sorpreso dalla mia gentilezza. ‘Sì,’ continuai; ‘non l’ho mai fatto prima.’”

L’ho già detto prima, perché mi vergognavo di farlo; ma ora lo dirò.

“Mi addolora molto, e potrebbe persino disgustarmi, se continui a soffrire in questo modo.”

L’abitudine finirà per prendere il sopravvento su di te, se non la controlli in [[motifs/time|tempo]].

Ma l’intero modo in cui ti comporti con Lady Lowborough non è…



<span class="atom-split" data-atom="chapter_27--part_02" data-title="The Tenant of Wildfell Hall — Chapter 27 (part 2)" data-chapter="Chapter 27" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="archetype/innocent,motif/blood,motif/dust,motif/love,motif/marriage,motif/nature,motif/night,motif/tears,motif/time,motif/well,concept/doubt,concept/honour,concept/longing,concept/nature,concept/wonder,character/arthur,character/hector,character/helen,character/lord_lowborough"></span>


referable to wine; and this [[motifs/night|night]] you knew perfectly [[motifs/well|well]] what you were

doing.”



“[[motifs/well|Well]], I’m sorry for it,” replied he, with more of sulkiness than

contrition: “what more would you have?”



“You are sorry that I saw you, no [[concepts/doubt|doubt]],” I answered coldly.



“If you had not seen me,” he muttered, fixing his eyes on the carpet,

“it would have done no harm.”



My heart felt ready to burst; but I resolutely swallowed back my

emotion, and answered calmly,



“You think not?”



“No,” replied he, boldly. “After all, what have I done? It’s

nothing—except as you choose to make it a subject of accusation and

distress.”



“What would [[characters/lord-lowborough|Lord Lowborough]], your _friend_, think, if he knew all? or

what would you yourself think, if he or any other had acted the same

part to me, throughout, as you have to Annabella?”



“I would blow his brains out.”



“[[motifs/well|Well]], then, [[characters/arthur|Arthur]], how can you call it nothing—an offence for which

you would think yourself justified in blowing another man’s brains out?

Is it nothing to trifle with your friend’s feelings and mine—to

endeavour to steal a woman’s affections from her husband—what he values

more than his gold, and therefore what it is more dishonest to take?

Are the [[motifs/marriage|marriage]] vows a jest; and is it nothing to make it your sport

to break them, and to tempt another to do the same? Can I [[motifs/love|love]] a man

that does such things, and coolly maintains it is nothing?”



“You are breaking your [[motifs/marriage|marriage]] vows yourself,” said he, indignantly

rising and pacing to and fro. “You promised to [[concepts/honour|honour]] and obey me, and

now you attempt to [[characters/hector|hector]] over me, and threaten and accuse me, and call

me worse than a highwayman. If it were not for your situation, [[characters/helen|Helen]], I

would not submit to it so tamely. I won’t be dictated to by a woman,

though she be my wife.”



“What will you do then? Will you go on till I hate you, and then accuse

me of breaking my vows?”



He was silent a moment, and then replied: “You never will hate me.”

Returning and resuming his former position at my feet, he repeated more

vehemently—“You cannot hate me as long as I [[motifs/love|love]] you.”



“But how can I believe that you [[motifs/love|love]] me, if you continue to act in this

way? Just imagine yourself in my place: would _you_ think I loved

_you_, if _I_ did so? Would you believe my protestations, and [[concepts/honour|honour]]

and trust me under such circumstances?”



“The cases are different,” he replied. “It is a woman’s [[concepts/nature|nature]] to be

constant—to [[motifs/love|love]] one and one only, blindly, tenderly, and for

ever—bless them, dear creatures! and you above them all; but you must

have some commiseration for us, [[characters/helen|Helen]]; you must give us a little more

licence, for, as Shakespeare has it—



However we do praise ourselves,

Our fancies are more giddy and unfirm,

More [[concepts/longing|longing]], wavering, sooner lost and won

Than women’s are.”





“Do you mean by that, that your fancies are lost to me, and won by Lady

Lowborough?”



“No! heaven is my witness that I think her mere [[motifs/dust|dust]] and ashes in

comparison with you, and shall continue to think so, unless you drive

me from you by too much severity. She is a daughter of earth; you are

an angel of heaven; only be not too austere in your divinity, and

remember that I am a poor, fallible mortal. Come now, [[characters/helen|Helen]]; won’t you

forgive me?” he said, gently taking my hand, and looking up with an

[[archetypes/innocent|innocent]] smile.



“If I do, you will repeat the offence.”



“I swear by—”



“Don’t swear; I’ll believe your word as [[motifs/well|well]] as your oath. I wish I

could have confidence in either.”



“Try me, then, [[characters/helen|Helen]]: only trust and pardon me this once, and you shall

see! Come, I am in hell’s torments till you speak the word.”



I did not speak it, but I put my hand on his shoulder and kissed his

forehead, and then burst into [[motifs/tears|tears]]. He embraced me tenderly; and we

have been good friends ever since. He has been decently temperate at

table, and [[motifs/well|well]]-conducted towards Lady Lowborough. The first day he

held himself aloof from her, as far as he could without any flagrant

breach of hospitality: since that he has been friendly and civil, but

nothing more—in my presence, at least, nor, I think, at any other [[motifs/time|time]];

for she seems haughty and displeased, and [[characters/lord-lowborough|Lord Lowborough]] is manifestly

more cheerful, and more cordial towards his host than before. But I

shall be glad when they are gone, for I have so little [[motifs/love|love]] for

Annabella that it is quite a task to be civil to her, and as she is the

only woman here besides myself, we are necessarily thrown so much

together. Next [[motifs/time|time]] Mrs. Hargrave calls I shall hail her advent as

quite a relief. I have a good mind to ask [[characters/arthur|Arthur]]’s leave to invite the

old lady to stay with us till our guests depart. I think I will. She

will take it as a kind attention, and, though I have little relish for

her society, she will be truly welcome as a third to stand between Lady

Lowborough and me.



The first [[motifs/time|time]] the latter and I were alone together, after that unhappy

evening, was an hour or two after breakfast on the following day, when

the gentlemen were gone out, after the usual [[motifs/time|time]] spent in the writing

of letters, the reading of newspapers, and desultory conversation. We

sat silent for two or three minutes. She was busy with her work, and I

was running over the columns of a paper from which I had extracted all

the pith some twenty minutes before. It was a moment of painful

embarrassment to me, and I thought it must be infinitely more so to

her; but it seems I was mistaken. She was the first to speak; and,

smiling with the coolest assurance, she began,—



“Your husband was merry last [[motifs/night|night]], [[characters/helen|Helen]]: is he often so?”



My [[motifs/blood|blood]] boiled in my face; but it was better she should seem to

attribute his conduct to this than to anything else.



“No,” replied I, “and never will be so again, I trust.”



“You gave him a curtain lecture, did you?”



“No! but I told him I disliked such conduct, and he promised me not to

repeat it.”



“I _thought_ he looked rather subdued this morning,” she continued;

“and you, [[characters/helen|Helen]]? you’ve been weeping, I see—that’s our grand resource,

you know. But doesn’t it make your eyes smart? and do you always find

it to answer?”



“I never cry for effect; nor can I conceive how any one can.”



“[[motifs/well|Well]], I don’t know: I never had occasion to try it; but I think if

Lowborough were to commit such improprieties, I’d make _him_ cry. I

don’t [[concepts/wonder|wonder]] at your being angry, for I’m sure I’d give my husband a

lesson he would not soon forget for a lighter offence than that. But

then he never _will_ do anything of the kind; for I keep him in too

good order for that.”



“Are you sure you don’t arrogate too much of the credit to yourself.

[[characters/lord-lowborough|Lord Lowborough]] was quite as remarkable for his abstemiousness for some

[[motifs/time|time]] before you married him, as he is now, I have heard.”



“Oh, about the _wine_ you mean—yes, he’s safe enough for that. And as

to looking askance to another woman, he’s safe enough for that too,

while I live, for he worships the very ground I tread on.”



“Indeed! and are you sure you deserve it?”



“Why, as to that, I can’t say: you know we’re all fallible creatures,

[[characters/helen|Helen]]; we none of us deserve to be worshipped. But are _you_ sure your

darling Huntingdon deserves all the [[motifs/love|love]] you give to _him?_”



I knew not what to answer to this. I was burning with anger; but I

suppressed all outward manifestations of it, and only bit my lip and

pretended to arrange my work.



“At any rate,” resumed she, pursuing her advantage, “you can console

yourself with the assurance that _you_ are worthy of all the [[motifs/love|love]] he

gives to you.”



“You flatter me,” said I; “but, at least, I can try to be worthy of

it.” And then I turned the conversation.
